pr_title: fix(localize): render ICU placeholders in extracted translation files
pr_body:
Previously placeholders were only rendered for dynamic interpolation
expressons in `$localize` tagged strings. But there are also potentially
dynamic values in ICU expressions too, so we need to render these as
placeholders when extracting i18n messages into translation files.

Fixes #38437

issue_context.title: New localize extractor tool: incorrect source/target with plural forms
issue_context.body:
# 🐞 bug report ### Affected Package The issue seems to be caused by package @angular/localize ### Is this a regression? No because it's a new tool, but yes because the old extractor worked. ### Description When using the new extractor tool introduced in https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/32912 (`./node_modules/.bin/localize-extract`), it seems to create an XLIFF 1.2 file with invalid `source` when using plural in templates. For example with the following template: ``` Updated {minutes, plural, =0 {just now} =1 {one minute ago} other {{{minutes}} minutes ago}} ``` It creates this element ``` {VAR_PLURAL, plural, =0 {just now} =1 {one minute ago} other {{INTERPOLATION} minutes ago}} ../app/app.component.html 1 ``` If we use the `source` as a `target`: ``` {VAR_PLURAL, plural, =0 {just now} =1 {one minute ago} other {{INTERPOLATION} minutes ago}} {VAR_PLURAL, plural, =0 {just now} =1 {one minute ago} other {{INTERPOLATION} minutes ago}} ../app/app.component.html 1 ``` Then we can't build the application: ``` Error: Unexpected character "EOF" (Do you have an unescaped "{" in your template? Use "{{ '{' }}") to escape it.) Error: Invalid ICU message. Missing '}'. ``` ## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction https://github.com/Chocobozzz/angular-test ## 🔥 Exception or Error 
Error: Unexpected character "EOF" (Do you have an unescaped "{" in your template? Use "{{ '{' }}") to escape it.)
Error: Invalid ICU message. Missing '}'.
## 🌍 Your Environment **Angular Version:** 
Angular CLI: 10.1.0-next.4
Node: 12.18.3
OS: linux x64

Angular: 10.1.0-next.5
... animations, common, compiler, compiler-cli, core, forms
... localize, platform-browser, platform-browser-dynamic, router
... service-worker
Ivy Workspace: Yes

-----------------------------------------------------------

rxjs                              6.6.2
typescript                        3.9.7
webpack                           4.44.1
**Anything else relevant?** The issue seems to be `{INTERPOLATION}`
comments: I tested the latest angular release and it works. Thanks @petebacondarwin for your work on localization, that allowed us to reduce our build time by 10 with reduced localized bundle sizes.
Fantastic! Great to hear your build time improvements. Is that 10 times faster?

> Fantastic! Great to hear your build time improvements. Is that 10 times faster?

Yes, ~1h20 before and now ~8 minutes. Before your new extractor we used [18n-polyfill](https://github.com/ngx-translate/i18n-polyfill/) to translate our components, requiring to make 1 Angular build per language (because it `require` the translated XLIFF file of the current locale). Now we do only 1 build :) We also reduced our bundle sizes since we don't need to `require` XLIFF files anymore.

The only (small) issue we have now, is that we use new IDs for strings in components and old IDs for strings in templates. So translators could have to translate twice the same string (because they don't have the same ID, even if there have the same source). But it's not a big deal, we'll wait the migration tool to migrate to new IDs :)
You can turn off legacy message ids for your project, and then have new ids everywhere: set `enableLegacyMessageIds` to false.

Yes I now but we need to update existing IDs to new ID format first to not loose existing translations.

For example, if I regenerate `angular.xlf` using `./node_modules/.bin/localize-extract` with `enableLegacyMessageIds: false`, and then merge this file in existing translations (`angular.fr.xlf`), we'll loose translated strings that used legacy IDs because they don't exist anymore in `angular.xlf`.
Right! I have a plan to work on a migration tool for these purposes when we look at deprecating and removing the legacy ids.
